A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PancapScore, PancapEngine, SA-Pancap, and PancapChain research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original captioning comparisons, stage ablations, retrieval results, image reconstructions, and an analysis of agreement with human judgments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds retrieval comparisons, expanded ablation results, and downstream VQA experiments using panoptic captions for pretraining.

M1.justification: The data engine, four-stage PancapChain procedure, autoregressive training objective, and inference sequence remain unchanged. Appendix E.1 expands their documentation; the new pretraining experiment uses the existing captioner without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds downstream visual question answering on VizWiz and ScienceQA, using LLaVA-1.5 training data and captions generated from SAM and COCO images. This substantially extends actual training and task coverage beyond v1's captioning, retrieval, and reconstruction evaluations.

E2.justification: Table A1 adds GIT and LLaVA-1.5 to the DOCCI captioner-based retrieval comparison. Their reported Recall@1 values are 16.7 and 55.4, respectively. The existing retrieval comparators and main SA-Pancap comparator set are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces a distinct pretraining-and-instruction-tuning evaluation using LLaVA-1.5-7B with LoRA. It compares 558K original pretraining samples against a size-matched mixture of 464K original plus 94K generated samples and an augmented mixture of 558K plus 94K. The original captioning and retrieval protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 Table A4 extends the existing stage ablation to test-set results and reports global-state and overall scores omitted from Table 4. Appendix G also adds a fixed-sample-count control testing whether pretraining gains depend solely on more data. The existing prompt and human-consistency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The 500-caption human-consistency study and its correlation-estimation procedures remain unchanged; the new experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantive downstream results: Table A5 reports VizWiz/ScienceQA scores of 47.8/68.4 for standard pretraining, 49.4/70.2 for the size-matched mixture, and 51.2/70.7 for augmented pretraining. It also adds retrieval-baseline scores and expanded stage-ablation results. These are new comparisons; the original Table 3 scores, including PancapChain's 175.75 validation and 173.19 test totals, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The PancapScore matching and aggregation definitions and PancapChain loss remain unchanged. Renumbering the appendix equation and expanding notation for training tuples restate existing mathematics rather than introducing new definitions, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same task, metric, benchmark, method contributions, and principal performance claims. The revised title and abstract's mention of broad applications do not materially change claims already made in v1.

C2.justification: New Appendix F explains limited global-state gains through the method's focus on individual entities. Appendix G interprets the fixed-size pretraining comparison as evidence that gains are not solely due to data quantity. The existing qualifications about approximate text equivalence and broader-impact limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 explicitly documents mixing four types of training tuples and expands their inputs, targets, and prompt construction. Appendix G specifies the new caption-generation sources and pretraining mixtures. Existing optimization settings, hardware information, and project access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a short comparison with scene-graph-based captioning. References are added for that discussion, GIT, the VQA benchmarks, and several broader applications, while the LLMDet citation is removed. The central positioning relative to detailed captioning and grounded MLLMs remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title and terminology, expands Appendix E.1, adds appendix sections for extended ablations and pretraining, and brings reconstruction discussion into the main text. These are localized edits and extensions; most prose and the main section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 expands Table A1 and adds Tables A4 and A5. New main-text Figure 4 redisplays two examples already present in v1 Figure A1, which remains in the appendix. Figure spacing, table placement, and pagination change, but the principal diagrams and overall visual format are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens evidence for downstream usefulness through the pretraining experiment, particularly its fixed-sample-count control, and provides fuller ablations and clearer training documentation. These gains are limited: the new transfer study covers one model and two benchmarks without uncertainty estimates, while the main method and results remain unchanged.
